text: All three commits are in and the tree is clean. Let me run the full suite once more with the race detector as a final verification:

Both halves of the report are addressed on branch `fix/files-upload-retry` (3 commits, all tests pass with `-race`, not pushed).

## Why uploads didn't retry

The retry transport can only re-send a request whose body is replayable — it requires `req.GetBody` to be set (`pipedrive/retry.go:86`). Go's `http.NewRequest` auto-populates `GetBody` only for `*bytes.Reader`, `*strings.Reader`, and `*bytes.Buffer`. Every JSON call in the SDK marshals into `bytes.NewReader`, which is why those retry fine. But `Files.Add` forwards the caller's reader verbatim into `Raw.Do`, so a body built around an `os.Open` file had no `GetBody`, `shouldRetry` returned false even for 429, and the rate-limit error surfaced immediately. `RetryAllMethods` was a red herring — it only gates 502/503/504, and 429 was already retryable for any method, just not with that body.

## What changed

**`fix(retry)` — `pipedrive/raw.go`:** `Raw.Do` now installs `GetBody` for any `io.ReadSeeker` body (an `*os.File`, for instance), rewinding to the body's initial offset per attempt. It also wraps the first attempt's body in `NopCloser`, because `net/http` closes each attempt's body and an `*os.File` would otherwise be closed before the replay — closing stays with the caller, matching the usual `defer f.Close()` pattern. Non-seekable streams remain non-replayable and are still not retried, which is now documented on `Do` and `Files.Add`. This also fixes `Files.Update` and any raw escape-hatch call with a file body.

**`feat(v1)` — `Files.Upload`:** a convenience method shaped like `CallLogs.AddRecording`:

```go
file, err := client.Files.Upload(ctx, "report.pdf", f,
    v1.WithUploadDealID(v1.DealID(42)))
```
